key_papers.summary: An antibody blocking the TLR4/MD-2 complex reduced colitis-associated neoplasia in mice, supporting that TLR4/MD-2 signalling promotes disease.
An antibody against the TLR4/MD-2 complex lessened DSS colitis early but impaired mucosal healing during recovery, so the net effect is mixed.
A small-molecule TLR4 inhibitor predicted to bind the MD-2 pocket reduced inflammation in endotoxemia and necrotizing enterocolitis models, but MD-2 itself was not directly perturbed.
Baicalein, which binds MD-2 and blocks MD-2/TLR4 complex formation, alleviated TNBS colitis in mice, suggesting MD-2 inhibition is beneficial.
